title: Molecular Biology Test for Rapid Detection of cagA Gene in H. pylori Isolates
author: Eliana Rocio Rodríguez Gómez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.54jg8un
materials: PCR amplification was carried out a volume of 50 µL containing 0.3 µM concentrations of primers (Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA, USA), 100 ng H. pylori genomic DNA and 1 U of master mix for Taq DNA polymerase (Promega, Madison, USA)
The polymerase chain reaction conditions included:

Samples which presented two or more bands in agarose gels from PCR amplifications (samples with mixed infection), were visualized and cut using an UV transilluminator. Each gel band with different size was put in an eppendorf tube and then purified using the Wizard SV Gel and PCR Clean- Up System Kit (Promega, Madison, USA), according to the manufacturer’s instructions. DNA concentration was determined by spectrophotometry using NanoDrop 2000 (Thermo Scientific, Wilmington, NC).

steps.title: Amplify cagA gene 3´ repeat regions
steps.instruction: Perform polymerase chain reaction (PCR) to amplify the entire 3´ repeat regions of the cagA gene using specific primers.

steps.title: Analyze PCR products via electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Analyze the PCR products using 2% agarose gel electrophoresis with Syber Safe and visualize using the Gel Doc XR+ system (Biorad, Hércules, CA, USA).

steps.title: Perform secondary amplification and sequencing
steps.instruction: Further amplify the DNA obtained from the gel bands via conventional PCR and sequence the products.

substeps.instruction: Sequence both DNA strands (forward and reverse sense) using the Sanger method
Use H. pylori reference strain (NCTC 11637) as a sequence control

steps.title: Perform bioinformatic analysis
steps.instruction: Align and analyze the nucleotide and peptide sequences.

substeps.instruction: Align nucleotide sequences using BLASTx, including H. pylori reference strain cagA sequences (NCTC 11637) (GenBank access AF202973)
Align deduced peptide sequences containing EPIYA motifs using CLUSTAL W (European Bioinformatics Institute)
